# Mission 1

## Hallway Analysis

A motion that could confuse or discomfort someone nearby would be if a robot suddenly started to back up without any signal, the way to fix this would be to remove backwards movement and take the extra actions to turn and than move forward, if the front of the robot is visible and obvious, the tradeoff being that it would just take longer. Doing a test to see if people jump or trip over the robot whenever it moves could be a way to measure its criteria for if it's a good robot or not.

## Trial Synthesis

The straight line trial was the one that matched my expectations the most as it was the simplest on, for the other path shapes the biggest differences was the heading as it always turned slightly less than expected. My initial thought of a cause was the timings may have been a little off as it stopped slightly early due to a difference in system settings where FPS could have an effect on it, evidence that could test this theory would be running the same movements on a different system that may be slower to see if the turning either appears even less/more or if there's no change. The straight line distance at the same speed for twice the duration would be 0.15 * (3*2) = 0.15 * 6 = 0.9m for the ideal model. However based on previous predictions it might stop slightly earlier around ~0.8m.
